assumptions: Source assumption: equal end-of-period payments with the first payment one full period after disbursement at a fixed per-period rate (UMD end-of-year convention).
Application profile: fully amortizing loan - the last payment extinguishes principal plus accrued interest; no fees, prepayments, or rate resets.
i is the effective rate per payment period; convert a quoted nominal APR with the effective-rate record before use.

gaps: Needs new quantity meanings: periodic_payment and periodic_rate (period_count exists but the payment-timing context is new); no current-runtime projection attempted.
Algebraic inverse-direction twin of the uniform-present-value framing; kept as its own record because the assignment requires the loan-payment direction with explicit end-of-period timing.

models.inverse_notes: P=A*((1+i)**n-1)/(i*(1+i)**n) needs i>0 and n>=1; checked 329.2 times the UPV factor at 12%/4 gives 999.9 within rounding. Substitution check at n=1: A=P*(1+i) exactly. Solving for i needs iteration and for n a logarithm, both unsupported by the scalar grammar, so those directions are untested. The i-to-0 limit branch A=P/n is a different expression, never a guard relaxation.
limitations: The zero-rate case i=0 is excluded by guard; its limit branch A=P/n is a separate expression stated here, not substituted silently.
Beginning-of-period (annuity-due) schedules need the distinct factor with an extra (1+i) multiple and are not covered.
Solving for the rate or term needs iteration or a logarithm, unsupported by the scalar grammar; closed forms only.

references.method: Source prints A=$329.2 for P=$1000, i=12%, n=4 under the explicit statement This is the case of loans (mortgages); recomputation gives 329.234, so tolerance covers the $0.1 rounding.
references.provenance: Published worked example in the UMD tutorial, Equal-Payment-Series Capital-Recovery Factor section

references.method: Expected rounded to cents (exact-form value 193.32802); independently verified by summing the 60 individually discounted payments, which returns the 10000.00 principal, instead of re-evaluating the closed form.
references.provenance: Independent derivation: term-by-term discounted-cash-flow summation from the source end-of-period mechanics

rejection_cases.reason: Zero periodic rate makes the denominator zero and needs the separate limit branch A=P/n; excluded by i>0.
Term count n is required; a payment cannot be sized without the number of periods.

relationship.translation_notes: Transcribed verbatim into scalar syntax; only bracket grouping changed. Dimensional check: USD times a dimensionless capital-recovery factor stays USD. Guards i>0 and n>=1 jointly imply the denominator (1+i)^n-1 is positive, preserving the pre-simplification exclusion. End-of-period timing carried from the source convention into the variable definitions. Reference exponents 4 and 60 are within the tooling cap. r2 context alignment: output A carries the :schedule-qualified context, marking it as the amortization-schedule payment consumed by the loan-payment-interest/principal-portion records; inputs P/i/n keep the loan-level context.
